A score is a claim about the future: roughly how well a model will predict data it has not
seen. The six pages in this section cover three ideas, on the same simulated survey as the
rest of the course, with linear regression, logistic regression and the random forest as
the models.

A score is only as honest as its folds:

- **cross-validation**: five or ten folds of sites give every station one out-of-fold
  prediction, and nested cross-validation scores a search for the best model as well as
  the model it picks;
- **spatial and temporal cross-validation**: a score says how well a model predicts
  stations as far from its fitted data as the held-out ones were, so blocks of the map
  test new areas, and a forecast is tested on later years.

The measure must follow the use:

- **regression performance measures**: RMSE, MAE and R² weigh errors their own way and
  can choose different models on skewed counts;
- **classification performance measures**: presence can be scored on the calls at one
  threshold, on how well the probabilities rank the stations, or on whether the
  probabilities can be read as chances;
- **choosing measures that match the objective**: a shortlist of stations is scored on
  the animals it finds, and the costs of misses and false alarms set the threshold.

A score needs an interval:

- **uncertainty and stability**: drawing the sites again puts an interval on a score, and
  a paired comparison says how sure a ranking of two models is.

The section picks up threads from earlier ones.
[Hyperparameter selection](../05-generalisation/hyperparameter-selection.qmd) chose a
setting by cross-validation by site; [Cross-validation](cross-validation.qmd) shows that
the folds that choose a model cannot also score it.
[Dependent data](../06-assumptions-limitations/dependent-data.qmd) found that visits to
one site repeat each other; [Spatial and temporal cross-validation](spatial-and-temporal-cv.qmd)
holds out blocks wide enough to keep a site's neighbours out of its training data, and
[Uncertainty and stability](uncertainty-and-stability.qmd) resamples whole sites to put an
interval on a score.
[Class imbalance](../06-assumptions-limitations/class-imbalance.qmd) showed that accuracy
hides the misses of a rare answer; [Classification performance measures](classification-metrics.qmd)
counts misses and false alarms apart, and
[Choosing measures that match the objective](choosing-a-metric.qmd) chooses the threshold
from what each costs.

## Further resources

**Documentation**

- [Evaluate your model with resampling](https://www.tidymodels.org/start/resampling/), tidymodels.
- [rsample](https://rsample.tidymodels.org/) and [yardstick](https://yardstick.tidymodels.org/), tidymodels. Every resampling scheme, and every metric with its definition.
- [Cross-validation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/cross_validation.html) and [metrics and scoring](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/model_evaluation.html), scikit-learn user guide. Its section on grouped data covers cross-validation by site.
